source_document.body:

VW ID. Cross Goes on Sale, Here’s How Much the Zero-Emission Baby SUV Costs
6 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
Subsequent to the official unveiling hosted this summer, the Volkswagen ID. Cross hit the assembly line at the Pamplona factory in Navarra, Spain, in September, and now it is ready to go on sale in the United Kingdom.
The company’s local branch recently announced that the order books will officially open on November 19, albeit for the 52 kWh battery pack versions, as the cheaper ones, which feature a 37 kWh battery pack will go on sale in January 2027.
Thus, the only versions that will be available starting later this week will be the Life and Style 52 kWh, with the former starting at 30,260 pounds (equal to $43,930) and the latter at 33,675 pounds ($44,480) on-the-road, including VAT. VW says that the 52 kWh models are eligible for the electric car grant (£1,500 / $1,980), and qualification for the 37 kWh versions is still awaiting confirmation.
As for the 37 kWh -equipped variants of the 2026/2027 Volkswagen ID. Cross , these will also be available in the Life and Style trim levels. Pricing for the former will kick off at 26,985 pounds ($35,640), OTR, including VAT, and the latter will start at 30,400 pounds ($40,150).
Photo: Volkswagen Volkswagen’s ID. Cross equipped with the 37 kWh battery pack can be charged at up to 88 kW, whereas the 52 kWh option can sip electrons at up to 105 kW. The lesser model is said to have a combined WLTP-rated range of 194 miles (312 km), and the superior one can travel up to 265 miles (426 km), the company says. A 10-80 percent recharge is said to take 23 minutes. The former has 135 ps (133 hp/99 kW) to play with, and the latter enjoys 211 ps (208 hp/155 kW).
Strangely, the press release shared at the bottom of the page does not reveal the equipment of the ID. Cross , and neither does the company’s official UK website. However, the configurator does, and that’s how we were able to find out that the model comes with stuff such as 7x18-inch alloys (Edinburgh), LED headlights, a reversing camera, keyless entry and go, a two-zone air conditioning system, a wireless charging pad, Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and ambient lighting.
The electric crossover also features four USB-C ports, two at the front and two at the rear, a six-speaker sound system, digital radio, a 12.9-inch infotainment screen, and plenty of safety gizmos. These include the automatic emergency braking with pedestrian and cyclist monitoring, adaptive cruise control, advanced driver attention and drowsiness monitoring, lane keeping assist, and others.
Opt for the Style trim level versions of the 2026/2027 Volkswagen ID. Cross , and the electric crossover will come with 8x19-inch alloys (Sevilla), LED matrix headlights, a navigation system, a heated multi-function steering wheel, sports comfort seats at the front with heating, and a 30-color ambient lighting system.
It also sports stainless steel pedals, the same sound system, infotainment, USB-C ports, auto-dimming rearview mirror, two-zone air conditioning system, reversing camera, front and rear parking sensors, and the same safety gizmos, the configurator reveals.
Photo: Volkswagen Things such as the energy-efficient heat pump, 3-pin charging cable, Technology Package (Style), rear tinted windows, panoramic glass roof, Seat Comfort Package, removable and lockable tow bar, Harman Kardon sound system, Mistral Crystal Gray-Natural White upholstery, and others are available.
Volkswagen’s ID. Cross is 4,153 mm (163.5 inches) long, which means that its footprint is similar to that of the T-Cross . However, it won’t cannibalize it, because the T-Cross is an ICE-powered model, whereas the ID. Cross is fully electric, as we already told you. It is built on the MEB+ construction, just like the ID. Tiguan, as well as the Cupra Raval, and the Skoda Epiq and Peaq.
The VW T-Cross, on the other hand, shares its old MQB A0 construction with the demised Audi A1, the SEAT Arona, Ibiza, Skoda’s Kamiq, Scala, Fabia, Slavia, the Mk6 VW Polo, and others.
Following in the footsteps of the ID. Polo and ID. Polo GTI , the Volkswagen ID. Cross is pretty much a high-riding alternative to the battery-electric Polo, and takes on the likes of the Renault 4 and Kia EV2. It offers 475 liters (16.8 cu-ft) of storage behind the rear seats, which is a 20-liter (0.7 cu-ft) improvement over the gasoline T-Cross, and the cargo area increases to 1,345 liters (47.5 cu-ft) with the rear seats folded down. The model has a towing rating of up to 1,200 kg (2,645 lbs).
As previously mentioned, the order books for the Volkswagen ID. Cross will officially open in the United Kingdom later this week, on November 19, 2026, albeit for the 52 kWh variants only, as the 37 kWh versions will go on sale in January 2027. And as you likely suspect, the car manufacturer does not intend to bring this model to the United States of America. But should they?
